page_placements.theme: Weak supervision beating strong training on gold or on the same labels (PGR above 1, OPR above 1)

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Applies weak-to-strong training to contextual decision-making and reports decision-risk results in synthetic newsvendor and comment-moderation tasks, a new setting for the claim. Its OPR compares W2S with a strong-only model, not with the weak supervisor, and is not Burns et al.'s PGR.
record.gate_note: The reported empirical results compare W2S with a strong-only benchmark using OPR (strong-only excess decision risk divided by W2S excess decision risk). They do not compare W2S performance with the weak supervisor or report PGR. The OPR results are retained as related findings, not as measurements of the claim versions. The paper also gives theoretical bounds and cites results from other work; cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study builds a decision-aware W2S pipeline for contextual stochastic optimization and reports only how its method compares with a strong model trained on the same scarce labels. It uses the OPR measure: strong-only excess decision risk divided by W2S excess decision risk. It never reports the weak teacher's decision risk, so it cannot show whether the student beats its supervisor (V1) or report PGR (V3). Its theory (Theorem 1, Corollary 1) gives sufficient conditions for W2S to beat strong-only training, not for the student to beat the supervisor (V5). This is a related but different construct, closer to semi-supervised learning than to the PGR question. The OPR findings are recorded under fits_no_version, not as tests. The reader's tests/T3 label is not supported.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that weak supervision can improve downstream decision performance over strong-only training when labels are scarce and unlabeled contexts are abundant. Representation overlap governs how much teacher error is inherited, and the experiments are described as consistent with the theory.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a weak model trained on limited labels to provide soft outcome-distribution supervision to a stronger model on unlabeled contexts. Unlike the original study's performance-gap-recovered measure and task evaluations, it optimizes and evaluates downstream decision risk and compares W2S with a strong-only model.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with labeled sample size n, unlabeled sample size N, and weak–strong representation overlap ds∧w; the moderation experiment reports no improvement for small N and OPR above one once N > 600.

fits_no_version.finding: In synthetic newsvendor and comment-moderation experiments, W2S has lower excess decision risk than strong-only training (OPR>1) when labels are scarce and unlabeled contexts are abundant. It is no better or worse at small N (R7, R8), and the gain narrows as n grows.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Decision-aware W2S beats strong-only training on scarce labels when unlabeled data are abundant.

fits_no_version.finding: The W2S advantage over strong-only falls as the correlation dimension between weak and strong representations rises, with OPR approaching 1 at high overlap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Greater weak–strong representation overlap reduces W2S benefit over strong-only training; this is an OPR analogue of V4's 'similar errors shrink gains'.

record.problems: The experiments compare W2S with a strong-only benchmark, not with the weak supervisor, and do not report PGR. The comment-moderation OPR uses a held-out empirical split because the ground-truth distribution is unavailable. Several outcomes are described qualitatively in the text rather than given as exact values.
record.rows_left_out: No findings omitted under the 60-row limit. The paper's theoretical bounds and cited results are not empirical rows.

untested.parts: No comparison of the W2S student with the weak teacher's decision risk; no PGR.
No auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling or loss variants against naive W2S.
No PGR as a function of model size or task. Overlap and sample-size effects are measured only through OPR against strong-only.
No exploitation of supervisor blind spots and no distribution shift. The overlap effect is measured on OPR, not PGR.
The theory bounds W2S against a strong-only benchmark, not against the supervisor.

record.verdict_notes: The weak teacher's own decision risk is never reported, so student-versus-supervisor results cannot be recovered from the text. The strong model's task pre-training compute was deliberately restricted. The comment-moderation data were augmented with Claude-generated severe-toxicity comments.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare the W2S student with the weak supervisor and does not report PGR.
Does not test auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling weak supervisors, or loss variants against naive fine-tuning.

Studies representation overlap, labeled and unlabeled sample sizes, and a decision-making task using OPR. It does not report PGR, compare model sizes as a PGR predictor, or test NLP, chess, or reward-modelling tasks.
Does not test distribution shift or whether similar model errors reduce PGR.
The theory gives sufficient conditions for W2S to improve decision risk over a strong-only benchmark; it does not establish conditions under which a student must beat its weak supervisor.
